original.reason: The asserted hierarchy is neither proved nor correct: for N=3, (3,2,1) uniquely determines outcomes but is excluded. Thus the Fibonacci conclusion is false.

judgment.reason: It correctly identifies (3,2,1) as a counterexample, but falsely claims (2,2,2) is unique: a directed 3-cycle of decisive results also gives (2,2,2).
Although (3,2,1) refutes the Fibonacci claim, (2,2,2) is not unique, since a cyclic set of three wins yields the same scores.
Its proposed all-draw counterexample is false: the decisive 3-cycle has score sequence (2,2,2). The separate (3,2,1) observation does refute the conclusion.
It incorrectly treats (2,2,2) as uniquely all draws; a three-team win cycle has the same sequence. Its (3,2,1) point still shows the original conclusion is false.
